tagline: Past old seabeds to a dam named for a drowned gorge.
intro: North out of Vernal, US 191 climbs into the Uinta Mountains through formations that hold the record of warm shallow seas and Sahara-like dune fields, some 770 million years of it. Dinosaur bones, sharks' teeth and seashells turn up in this rock near Steinaker and Red Fleet. Then the road switchbacks to nearly 8,400 feet through aspen and pine and comes down toward Flaming Gorge.

There it forks. One branch crosses the dam to Dutch John and runs on to Wyoming. The other follows SR-44 along the south side of the reservoir and winds down through Sheep Creek Gap to Manila, a town named in 1898 for a naval victory on the far side of the Pacific.

moments.title: Flaming Gorge Dam
moments.text: The road crosses the top of a 502-foot concrete arch set in Red Canyon. The gorge John Wesley Powell named for its flaming red rock lies under the reservoir, almost 20 miles upstream.

moments.title: Dutch John
moments.text: Built by the Bureau of Reclamation in 1957 for the dam crews, once home to 3,500 people and now to about 140, plus the world's largest fishing fly, 32 feet long.

moments.title: Sheep Creek
moments.text: Back on the Manila branch, bighorn sheep can be seen on the rocks above the creek, and its cottonwoods and willows hold more kinds of migrating songbirds than any other spot in Utah.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Ashley National Forest, Scenic Byways and Backways
